company_stage: large public retail, ecommerce, and supply chain company

culture_principles.name: Public mission and customer-impact alignment
culture_principles.description: Walmart fit should connect work to the company outcomes and users described in cited public sources.

culture_principles.name: Evidence-backed execution
culture_principles.description: Strong answers should show practical judgment, clear tradeoffs, ownership, and outcomes rather than generic enthusiasm.

culture_principles.name: Customer price leadership as the constraint
culture_principles.description: Public material ties the business to everyday low prices, which makes cost-to-serve and waste reduction central to nearly every role.

culture_principles.name: Scale operations with local accountability
culture_principles.description: The company publicly operates through stores, clubs, and market-level leadership, so decisions balance central standards with local execution reality.

culture_principles.name: Technology in service of stores and supply chain
culture_principles.description: Public positioning frames automation and data work around store and supply-chain outcomes rather than technology for its own sake.

hiring_signals.signal: Connects decisions to the users, customers, products, or markets named in public company sources.
Uses concrete examples to show ownership, learning, and measurable improvement.
Reasons about cost, throughput, and inventory with concrete numbers from a real operation.
Shows a change rolled out across many locations that survived frontline reality and local variation.
Connects a technical or data initiative to a measured store, associate, or customer outcome.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Generic admiration for the company without a concrete role, customer, product, or business mechanism.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public lens usage should stay grounded in cited source signals and role-relevant evidence.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Treating Walmart as only retail store operations and ignoring supply chain, technology, and corporate functions.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public sources describe a large set of distinct role families.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Proposing a process or technology change without accounting for frontline labour and store variation.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Scale execution is a public operating promise, so an unqualified rollout claim cannot be evaluated.

interview_patterns.pattern: Use cited public source signals to test role-relevant judgment, ownership, communication, and impact.

honest_limits: This is a lightweight public-source lens and does not represent an official Walmart hiring standard.
It contains source metadata and non-verbatim public-safe signals only.
Role, team, seniority, location, and hiring manager can materially change interview emphasis.
This lens requires deeper multi-source validation before being promoted to FULLY_DISTILLED.
